The verified strict rational inequalities in the result follow, and 2π/7 is strictly between 0.8975979 and 0.8975980. Differentiating each flight and matching velocities at a transverse interface gives the stated exponential multiplier. Lower exterior time decreases under scalar order and upper time increases, proving the sign of P'−1 throughout each interval and thus uniqueness and stability there. The half-period map Q(y)=−x(π;y) is strictly decreasing, P=Q², and the central fixed point of Q is below all three intervals. Independently bracketing it in [−0.579024,−0.579021] bounds half-period exterior time below π/7, proving central repulsion. The three distinct Q-partners lie below the central solution, preserve the multipliers by the chain rule, and transversality and P'≠1 give local parameter continuation.
